name: Alabama

programs.name: Alabama Student Assistance Program (ASAP)
programs.summary: Need-based grant for Alabama residents at about 80 Alabama colleges, decided from the FAFSA. Each college has a fixed amount, so file as soon as the FAFSA opens.

award.summary: $300 to $5,000 a year, set by the college.

programs.name: Alabama Student Grant Program
programs.summary: A grant (not based on need) for Alabama residents at a short list of eligible private Alabama colleges.

programs.name: Alabama G.I. Dependent Scholarship
programs.summary: For children, stepchildren and spouses of Alabama veterans with a 40% or higher service-connected rating: in-state tuition plus books at Alabama public colleges.

award.summary: In-state undergraduate tuition (up to a per-credit limit) plus up to $1,000 a semester for books and fees, after other aid.

aid_steps.title: File early for Alabama's need-based grant
aid_steps.summary: Alabama's ASAP grant comes from a fixed amount at each college, handed out first come, first served from the FAFSA.
how: Submit the FAFSA as soon as it opens in senior year.
List every Alabama college you're considering on the FAFSA so each one can offer ASAP.
Ask each college's aid office if it has its own scholarship application and deadline.

counselor_notes: Alabama has no statewide merit scholarship like HOPE. The big merit money comes from the colleges themselves: many Alabama public universities give automatic scholarships for GPA and ACT or SAT scores, with early deadlines (often December 1 to February 1). Always check each college's own scholarship page.

Alabama's need-based grant (ASAP) comes from the FAFSA; file it as soon as it opens. Dual enrollment scholarships at Alabama community colleges can cover college classes in high school (ask the school counselor).
